title: Don’t lose your data in a tunnel – DT Swiss adds Wahoo’s Trackr Speed tech to its hubs for GPS-free distance and speed
content:
Cyclist
Don’t lose your data in a tunnel – DT Swiss adds Wahoo’s Trackr Speed tech to its hubs for GPS-free distance and speed

DT Swiss has worked with Wahoo to develop a version of the Trackr Speed that can be integrated into its hubs. It incorporates a three-axis accelerometer that allows it to produce data on speed based on wheel rotation and so provides data to a head unit even when there’s no GPS signal.

For GPS to work, your cycling computer needs to have a signal from at least four GPS satellites. DT Swiss cites riding through tunnels or between mountains – very Swiss problems – or in cities with tall buildings as situations in which GPS signal may be lost, so you’ll not have accurate positional or speed data.

The Wahoo Trackr Speed sensor, on which DT Swiss’s tracker is based, is fixed to the outside of your front hub and transmits wheel rotation data to your head unit. It’s powered by a replaceable CR2032 battery with 200 hours claimed runtime and Wahoo says it weighs 13g.

The DT Swiss Trackr Speed incorporates Wahoo’s Trackr Speed tech into the inside of DT’s rear wheel hub, with a rechargeable battery to keep it running, recharged via a magnetic charging cable. It’s available as an add-on in the Spline and Dicut hubs, without adding extra bulk to them. It transmits to cycling computers, smartwatches and smartphones over both ANT+ and Bluetooth.  

DT Swiss will sell its Trackr Speed as a stand-alone product, priced at €59.90 (approx £51.50) and says it is compatible with most of its wheelsets. It can also be bought as a bundle with the G 1800 Spline wheelset.
